title: Offering and Asking for Help
summary: Offering help, asking for help, and reacting appropriately.
whyItMatters: Help exchanges are useful when someone is lost, cannot carry something, does not understand a machine, or needs practical information. A complete exchange identifies the problem, makes a clear request or offer, agrees on an action, and closes politely.

mentalModel.title: Notice, offer, specify
mentalModel.content: When offering help, first signal availability, then ask what is needed: 'Kann ich Ihnen helfen? Was suchen Sie?'

mentalModel.title: Make the request actionable
mentalModel.content: A useful request names the task, object, or information: 'Können Sie mir den Weg zum Bahnhof zeigen?'

mentalModel.title: Confirm the next action
mentalModel.content: Before closing, make the solution explicit: 'Wir fahren zusammen mit dem Bus. Er kommt in fünf Minuten.'

ruleBlocks.title: Offer help with a direct question
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Kann ich Ihnen helfen?' formally or 'Kann ich dir helfen?' informally.

ruleBlocks.title: Ask for one concrete action
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Können Sie mir bitte helfen?' and add the task or information you need.

ruleBlocks.title: Accept or decline clearly
ruleBlocks.content: Accept with 'Ja, bitte' or 'Das wäre nett'. Decline with 'Nein, danke. Es geht schon.'

ruleBlocks.title: Check and close
ruleBlocks.content: Repeat the important detail, ask a short confirmation question, and finish with thanks.

tables.title: Conversation Toolkit

tables.title: From Problem to Solution
rows: Ich suche den Bahnhof. Können Sie mir den Weg zeigen?
Können Sie mir das auf dem Stadtplan zeigen?
Soll ich Ihnen mit der Tasche helfen?

patterns: Können Sie / Kannst du mir bitte helfen?
Vielen Dank für Ihre / deine Hilfe.
sentenceStructure: Choose formal 'Sie/Ihnen' with strangers and informal 'du/dir' with familiar people.
Use a modal question to soften a request or offer.
Name the concrete problem after the opening phrase.
Close by confirming the solution or thanking the helper.

concepts: explain a simple problem and confirm a solution
offer nuanced advice and conditional assistance

comparisons.summary: The city lesson supplies realistic problems such as finding a destination, reading a route, or choosing transport.
The preposition lesson helps specify when and how the solution happens.

rows: Der Bus kommt in fünf Minuten.
Nach der Ampel gehen Sie rechts.
Sie können mit der U-Bahn fahren.

examples.de: A: Entschuldigung, können Sie mir helfen? Ich suche den Bahnhof. B: Ja, natürlich.
examples.en: A: Excuse me, can you help me? I am looking for the station. B: Yes, of course.

examples.de: A: Kann ich Ihnen mit der Tasche helfen? B: Ja, bitte. Das wäre sehr nett.
examples.en: A: Can I help you with the bag? B: Yes, please. That would be very kind.

examples.de: A: Können Sie mir das auf dem Stadtplan zeigen? B: Gern. Wir sind hier.
examples.en: A: Can you show me that on the city map? B: Gladly. We are here.

examples.de: A: Brauchst du Hilfe? B: Nein, danke. Es geht schon.
examples.en: A: Do you need help? B: No, thank you. I can manage.

examples.de: A: Also mit dem Bus bis zum Rathaus? B: Genau. Dort steigen Sie aus.
examples.en: A: So by bus as far as the town hall? B: Exactly. You get off there.

commonMistakes.wrong: Kann ich Ihnen helfen? Was brauchst du?
commonMistakes.correct: Kann ich Ihnen helfen? Was brauchen Sie?
commonMistakes.reason: Keep formal or informal address consistent within the exchange.
The verb 'helfen' takes a dative person: mir, dir, Ihnen.

commonMistakes.correct: Können Sie mir bitte den Weg zum Bahnhof zeigen?
commonMistakes.reason: A specific request tells the other person what action is needed.

commonMistakes.wrong: Leave immediately after receiving the information.
commonMistakes.correct: Repeat the key detail and say 'Vielen Dank'.
commonMistakes.reason: Confirmation checks accuracy and closes the exchange politely.

specialCases: 'Soll ich ...?' is a common way to offer a specific action and can be learned as a fixed chunk before 'sollen' is studied fully.
'Das wäre nett' uses a conditional form but functions well as a polite fixed response.
In an urgent emergency, direct language is appropriate: 'Hilfe!' or 'Rufen Sie bitte die Polizei!'
tips: Practice the same situation once formally and once informally.
Replace vague 'help' with a visible action: show, carry, explain, call, or wait.
Repeat one route or timing detail before thanking the helper.

memoryHooks.title: Problem, action, confirmation
memoryHooks.content: Name what is wrong, request or offer one action, then confirm what happens next.

memoryHooks.title: Help reaches mir
memoryHooks.content: Remember the common pair 'mir helfen' to anchor the dative person.
